name: Neo-Brutalist
summary: Hard shadows, ink outlines, stickers and a ticker: loud neo-brutalist cards that press on every beat.
look: Off-white paper with a 72 px grid, 5 px ink outlines, hard offset shadows, flat amber/teal/coral fills, taped cards, rotated stickers, 16-point starbursts and one scrolling ticker strip.

components.name: Heavy card
components.role: 5 px ink outline + 9 px hard offset shadow, no blur, r14

components.name: Press
components.role: card translates into its own shadow in 80–120 ms, always on a beat

components.name: Block headline
components.role: Manrope 800 uppercase on flat fills (white, amber, teal, soft teal, coral)

components.name: Sticker + starburst
components.role: rotated 2–8°, slapped on with 1.3 → 1 + wobble; starbursts only for errors and one stat

components.name: Tape
components.role: soft-teal strips with dashed edges holding cards to the page

components.name: Ticker strip
components.role: the only continuously moving element: a coral/ink band scrolling left

motion.name: Slam-in
motion.how: y −120 → 0 on steps(3) at 12 fps, 0.25 s, landing on the beat; no easing curves

motion.name: Press
motion.how: translate(9 px, 9 px) + shadow 9 → 0 in 0.1 s, then back in 0.1 s — the “click” on every downbeat (every 2 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Ticker
motion.how: linear x scroll at 1 bar per 480 px (240 px/s) for the whole scene — the constant against the stepped hits

story: Hook: “How many dashboards did you check today?” slams in as blocks over a pile of taped metric cards and a “38 tabs” starburst. Reveal: the pile presses flat on the drop; “You ship.” and “Pulse watches.” slam in and the Acme Pulse card drops. Proof: metric cards press in with ✓ stickers until the Checkout conversion card pops out coral with −18% (since 09:42 · after deploy #2231) and a cursor clicks ROLL BACK while the ticker scrolls. CTA: taped lockup card, tagline blocks, a “14 metrics” star and a heavy coral Start free button.
adapt: Turn your product’s key objects into heavy cards and let the one that needs attention pop out with a starburst; your CTA is simply the heaviest card in the film.

references.note: NN/G: neobrutalism definition and usability cautions
Config 2024 identity: shapes and motion principles (shift, transform)

fit.risk: Loud style can undercut trust for data products; keep the grid rigid and numbers untilted.
